criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, acidification), single-sat justification, and users (CSIRO/BOM, Aus Gov/university) all explained with references. Could be more detailed on customers vs operator but meets all 4 points.

evidence.quote: Earth observation satellite – specifically for coral reef and ocean monitoring
only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle justified with trade analysis, SSO LEO defined with altitude, inclination, a, e, RAAN, argument of latitude, STK screenshots Images 1-5; ground station Mt Pleasant with access report and communication stats; duration 5yr and drag-sail EOL covered. Strong evidence, minor simplification of J2.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous.
Average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved, in addition to the already frequent amount of passes.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion synthesizes launch, SSO orbit, ground contact and EOL, links back to bleaching problem, notes Vega E risk and alternative Vega C. Appropriate and detailed from body evidence.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.
Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory is well-located to receive data from this orbit type constantly

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Report has required sections and STK tables/figures, but figure captions inconsistent, some OCR table artefacts, grammar flaws, and uses Wikipedia despite prohibition, with inconsistent referencing style. Readable but not fully professional.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite

technical_issues.issue: Describes SSO maintenance as J2 perturbation causing RAAN precession of 1 deg/day, but imprecise phrasing; inclination vs altitude calc shown as Image 3 without derivation.
Uses argument of latitude u in COE table to handle circular orbit, but lists RAAN 27.33 deg as launch site location without stating LTAN/ LTDN.
Access report duplicates entry 14-15 same timestamp indicating STK export error; mean duration calculated but contact analysis does not link to Great Barrier Reef imaging windows.

overall: Solid SSO coral-reef mission with consistent launch/orbit/ground analysis and STK evidence. Good intro and conclusion. Presentation weakened by Wikipedia citation and figure labelling. EOL drag-sail appropriate for no-propulsion CubeSat class.

feedback.summary: You delivered a solid SSO coral-reef monitoring mission with clear rationale, a single-satellite approach, Vega E from Guiana, 600 km SSO with STK evidence, and Mt Pleasant ground analysis. Strengths are consistent design and good use of Images 1-5. Presentation limits your score due to figure labelling and Wikipedia use.
next_steps: Fix report presentation: add consistent, descriptive captions to all STK figures/tables (Images 1-5) and check referencing - replace Wikipedia in Bibliography with primary sources and apply a consistent citation style.
In Orbit, explicitly state LTAN/LTDN for your RAAN=27.33 deg, and add the J2 SSO formula linking 97.7924 deg inclination at 600 km to 1 deg/day RAAN precession instead of Image 3 alone.
In Ground Control & Communications, clean the access report duplicate entry 14-15 and link your 10-minute average contact stats directly to Great Barrier Reef imaging and downlink windows.

criteria.C1: You met all four intro points well. You explained coral-reef fluid-lensing as primary mission, bleaching rationale, why one satellite for simplicity, and CSIRO/BOM as users. For a stronger Accomplished, separate operator vs customers with roles and add literature support.
criteria.C2: Strong Accomplished work. You justified Vega E from Guiana Space Centre, defined SSO LEO with 600 km, e~0, i=97.7924°, a, RAAN, and argument of latitude u, with Images 1-5, plus Mt Pleasant access and 5-yr drag-sail EOL. Next, clarify J2 maintenance phrasing and LTAN.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion synthesises launch, polar SSO for consistent illumination, Mt Pleasant contact, and EOL, and notes Vega E risk with Vega C alternative. Well tied to evidence. To lift further, add quantitative takeaways from Orbit and Ground Control sections.
criteria.C4: You have clear structure and Executive Summary plus STK tables, but figure captions are inconsistent and Bibliography uses Wikipedia which was prohibited, with inconsistent style. For Accomplished, standardise captions/labels, proof grammar, and ensure text references match list.
